Good News: Jury Nullification is Interfering With Cannabis Convictions

The doctrine is premised on the idea that ordinary citizens, not government officials, should have the final say as to whether a person should be punished. As Adams put it, it is each juror’s “duty” to vote based on his or her “own best understanding, judgment and conscience, though in direct opposition to the direction of the court.”

This is the last remnant of juries having the ability to decide on the validity of the law itself. That power has systemically been removed from juries by the separation of legal issues into issues of law and issues of fact. Juries only handle issues of fact. And the legislature and judiciary controls issues of law. This division is terribly abused and is one good reason to be terrified of the legal system. There are even laws preventing defense attorneys from informing juries about jury nullification, which prevents jurors from ever realizing they have this limited power to decide against the laws they see as illegitimate. Once again, I'd like to direct people to look into sortition as applied to legislatures as a possible way to address legislative capture by monied interests.
